purpose: diagnose calibration needs in the first broad full-stack PIT LD-RC replay; analysis only, no parameter selected

attribution.conclusion: raw Wealth Core does not explain the PIT performance loss; controller/breadth timing is the primary recalibration domain

crisis_witnesses.interpretation: PIT breadth delayed FAST; PIT eventually fired on 2008-07-08
PIT missed early FAST and entered late SLOW near a rebound
one damaged holding out of 20 separated FAST protection from no FAST protection; PIT later entered SLOW after most drawdown had occurred
FAST remains effective when PIT breadth is unambiguously extreme

pit_metadata_coverage.caveat: coverage measured on active current-TICKERS common/listing projection, not the exact eligible or held population
pit_metadata_coverage.structural_effect: missing SIC becomes UNKNOWN:<security>, effectively disabling shared sector contagion for that security; missing CIK also creates singleton issuer authority

fast_acceleration_version_alignment.conclusion: main's historical 0.40 threshold is not portable to the current PIT breadth domain; the current 0.30 retained value performs better but is not considered calibrated

ldrc_recovery_diagnostic.interpretation: there is some recovery-timing headroom, but it is much smaller than the native breadth/controller issue and is not first priority

universe_geometry.reason: broad replay intentionally does not apply exchange gate because causal historical exchange authority is unavailable
universe_geometry.calibration_implication: freeze intended broad PIT eligibility domain before tuning leadership/recovery thresholds

priority_order: P0 freeze intended broad PIT eligibility/security-type/exchange domain
P0 stabilize PIT sector/issuer authority or make breadth explicitly coverage-aware/taxonomy-robust
P0 create one explicit PIT controller version; do not blindly import old FAST 0.40 or treat retained 0.30 as final
P1 calibrate FAST damaged-breadth level, damaged-breadth acceleration and sector-stress interaction under the frozen PIT domain
P1 re-evaluate SLOW only after FAST is recalibrated; 2010/2018 SLOW problems are largely downstream of missed FAST
P2 evaluate recovery ramp and LD-RC divergence/recovery timing
P2 normalize leadership population/top-fraction if the broad eligible population remains materially larger than the original domain
P3 instrument trade-level exit reasons before changing stop/review/cooldown
P3 calibrate execution/capacity separately from signal calibration

calibration_window_policy.note: 1998-2005 has already been observed for baseline performance, so it is a locked historical holdout, not a pristine never-seen sample
